newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai zero coupon bond auction seen next week.
newsitem.headline: Thai zero coupon bond auction seen next week.

text.p: Thailand will launch its first auction of zero coupon bonds to raise funds to help the troubled and cash-strapped property and financial sectors sometime next week, a senior central bank official said on Friday.
"There is definitely no auction of zero coupon bonds today and there will be one sometime next week. I cannot comment on the amount to be auctioned," the official told Reuters.

Some Thai officials had said earlier this week after the cabinet agreed to auction up to 50 billion baht of such bonds in tranches that up to one billion baht of the bonds would be auctioned on Friday (May 2).

But the central bank official said he had not been informed that the auction would be held today and that there might have been a misconception about the auction date. "We did not say that there would be an auction today," he said.
Proceeds from the bonds with seven-year maturity would be used to purchase non-performing property loans from banks and finance companies, aiding cash-strapped property firms.
The bond issue is to be managed by the government-run Property Loans Management Organisation.
